idiom_name: interface structs of function pointers + specification-keyed role table (GObject-style)
implementation_notes: Plain C has no classes and no dynamic dispatch, so the Component interface becomes a struct whose first member points to a table of function pointers, and a ComponentRole is a struct embedding the same interface plus a void* core that forwards each operation to it. GObject encodes exactly this discipline in its type system (register a non-instantiatable GInterface with G_DEFINE_INTERFACE, implement it via G_IMPLEMENT_INTERFACE, and check it at runtime with g_type_is_a / G_TYPE_CHECK_INSTANCE_CAST), which is the route to take when GLib's properties, signals and lifetime machinery are already part of the stack. For a small, fixed role set, a hand-rolled role table with static creators is closer to the metal and avoids the GType dependency; the full registry pays off only when roles are added later without recompiling the core.
pitfalls: Every role's vtable must be fully initialized; an unset forwarding slot is a null-pointer call at runtime, not a compile error.
Ownership is manual: the core must free all role records in its destructor and roles must not be freed separately, or the program double-frees.
Casts between a role struct and the interface struct are unchecked; keep the interface struct as the first member and cast only at controlled boundaries.
